title: EA关闭Mass Effect、Dragon Age缔造者BioWare，结束30年游戏开发

EA closes Mass Effect, Dragon Age creator BioWare after 30 years of game development
EA is reportedly laying off 400 employees, 50 of whom were the remaining staffers at BioWare.
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
October 21, 2026
schedule
4 Min Read
Image via BioWare/EA
Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and
Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
developer BioWare is shutting its doors after thirty years of game development.
The storied studio—which was
acquired by Electronic Arts
in 2007 through VG Holding Corp—announced the news in
a post on social media
. "There is nothing easy about writing those words," the statement reads. "Our focus right now is on our incredibly talented team who put their hearts into these games, and supporting one another through this transition." Bloomberg News
also reports
that EA is also laying off 400 employees, 50 of whom were working at BioWare on a new entry in the Mass Effect series.
According to Bloomberg, those other 400 layoffs come with the cancelation, downsizing, and reprioritization of other projects. A planned entry in the Sims series code-named "Project Lotus" has been canceled, while another game code-named "Project Evergreen" is being prioritized. It's also diverting resources away from Full Circle Studios' online skateboarding game
skate
while still maintaining active development on the game. Respawn and DICE studios are apparently set to collaborate on a new game which is "likely" to be another entry in the Star Wars: Battlefront series.
Related:
Innersloth co-founder warns devs: 'there are some very bad deals out there'
EA chief operating officer David Tinson and chief studios officer Cam Weber apparently sent a letter to EA staff saying that these decisions followed a "hard look at the business" that took place over the last several months. "Across our portfolio, we’re making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth," the letter said.
These layoffs come a few months after a joint investor group including the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund (PIF), Silver Lake and Affinity Partners
purchased EA
in a $55 billion transaction. Many developers
criticized
the purchase, with EA employees telling GameDeveloper.com that they only received "
vague reassurances"
about the company's future after the deal closed. Despite promises that EA would continued to "operate independently" under its new corporate ownership, workers expressed concern about the possible influence the deal would give Saudi government.
One anonymous employee expressed fear that layoffs or cuts would be inevitable for underperforming teams. "It's hard to see how teams or games that underperform wouldn't be dissolved or sold off," they said.
From
Shattered Steel
to
Dragon Age: The Veilguard
Founded in 1995 by Ray Muzkya, Greg Zeschuk, and Augustine Yip, BioWare's first game to hit the market was the 1997 mech combat simulation game
Shattered Steel
. In 1998, the Edmonton-based studio released the Dungeons & Dragons-themed title
Baldur's Gate
, the first of many interactive role-playing games inspired by tabletop game systems that would define its oeuvre for three decades. The most recent entry in the series,
Baldur's Gate III
, was developed by Larian Studios.
Related:
Griffin Gaming Partners, Entertainment 360 jointly unveil production company Hitpoint Entertainment
After moving on from Dungeons & Dragons, BioWare went on to develop
Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
and
Jade Empire
, each game winning exceptional praise from critics and players alike. It continued its run of hits with the release of
Mass Effect
in 2007 and
Dragon Age: Origins
in 2009, each kicking off a series of games with multiple sequels and spin-offs. A new division of the company was spun up in Austin, TX to develop
Star Wars: The Old Republic
, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG) now
owned and operated
by Broadsword.
After the 2014 release of
Dragon Age: Inqusition
, BioWare began to struggle as its parent company began to prioritize multiplayer live service games (that's according to former executive producer Mark Darrah, who has chronicled his time at BioWare on
his YouTube channel
). It released the single-player game
Mass Effect: Andromeda
in 2018, which failed to earn the same praise as BioWare's earlier work, and then would become the subject of investigative reports that
detailed a troubled development process
(EA has never provided public sales numbers for this title).
Related:
Ubisoft to close Trials studio RedLynx, downsize Ubisoft Singapore
The company began work on an online science fiction RPG that would become the 2019 title
Anthem
, which failed to gain traction as a long-lasting live service game,
only going on to sell around 5 million copies
before being shut down. Its development became
entangled
with work on the next Dragon Age game, which at first was set to be a single-player role-playing game, then was planned as a live service title, before eventually being reworked as a single-player game that would hit the market in 2024 called
Dragon Age: The Veilguard
.
As work finished on
The Veilguard
, EA announced that BioWare would begin work on a new game in the Mass Effect series. In the post announcing its closure, the studio confirmed that said game has now been canceled.
